guide: Component Guide Human View Machine View Overview Drawer is a panel that slides in from a screen edge above a dimmed backdrop, for tasks that need more room than a Modal but shouldn't fully interrupt the page layout behind it - the page stays visible and contextually present at the edge, unlike Modal's fully centered takeover. When to Use An edit-in-place panel - editing a record's details without leaving the list behind it. A filter or settings side panel - adjusting options while keeping the underlying content in view. A detail preview or a multi-step form that needs more room than a dialog - still tied to the specific context it opened from. When Not to Use A short, focused decision or confirmation - use Modal - Drawer's larger size is unnecessary weight for a quick yes/no. Content meant to persist as part of the page's normal layout - use a permanent panel or sidebar rather than a Drawer that must be explicitly opened and closed. A brief, non-blocking status update - use Toast or Notification instead of a full sliding panel. Best Practices Keep the underlying page visible and dimmed, not hidden, so context isn't lost while the Drawer is open. Choose a consistent edge (commonly the right) for a given type of task across the product. Warn before closing a Drawer with unsaved changes, the same way you would for a Modal. Do and Don't Do FiltersStatus, owner and date range - applied to the list still visible behind. A side task with enough substance to fill the panel, kept beside the list it acts on rather than covering it. Don't Discard draft?CancelDiscard A one-line confirmation leaves most of the panel empty and still blocks the page to slide in. Use Modal or Pop Confirm when there is only a question to ask. Accessibility Traps keyboard focus within the panel while open, and restores it to the triggering element on close, matching Modal's behavior. Exposed as role="dialog" with aria-modal="true" and an accessible name (its title via aria-labelledby), announced as it opens - like Modal, this is focus management and an interrupting dialog, not a passive aria-live announcement. Escape and a visible close control are both always available, regardless of what task is in progress inside it.
